land.text: Kandahar, where Ahmad Shah was crowned on 23 July 1747, and Ghazni, taken 'with little opposition'

predecessors.note: The Durrani page lists Afsharid Iran, the Mughal Empire, Maratha India and the Khanate of Bukhara as predecessors; Herat (late 1750) and Khorasan (1750-55) also came from the Afsharid successors.

land.text: Kabul (October 1747) and Peshawar (1747-48), taken from the Mughal-appointed governor Nasir Khan; the Punjab, Multan and Kashmir followed in 1752
the Principality of Kabul: 'The Sadozai rulers controlled little more than Kabul and its surroundings within about 160 km by 1818'; the Barakzai superseded the Durrani at Kabul in March 1823

successors.note: The Emirate of Afghanistan page gives 'Established: 1823' and 'Predecessor: Durrani Empire'.

land.text: Kandahar, founded by Sher Dil Khan in August 1818 'as a breakaway from the Durrani Empire'

successors.note: No dossier exists yet; Cliopatria has no row.

land.text: Herat, held by the Sadozai Mahmud Shah and Kamran Shah from 1818; the page lists the Kingdom of Herat among the Durrani successors

successors.note: No dossier exists yet; Cliopatria has no row.

land.text: Multan (1818), the Kashmir Valley (1819) and the Peshawar valley as a tributary (1823)

capitals.name: Kandahar
capitals.note: Infobox 'Kandahar (1747-1776)'; Ahmad Shah was crowned near Kandahar on 23 July 1747.

capitals.name: Kabul
capitals.note: Infobox 'Kabul (1776-1823)' with 'Peshawar as winter capital (1776-1823)' and 'Herat (1793-1863)'. The Timur Shah page says he 'formally established' Peshawar 'as the imperial capital in place of Kandahar' without a year.

rulers.name: Ahmad Shah Durrani
rulers.note: July 1747 to 16 October 1772 (the Ahmad Shah page gives 17 October).

rulers.name: Timur Shah
rulers.note: November 1772 to 20 May 1793 (his own page gives 18 May in the body).

rulers.name: Zaman Shah
rulers.note: 20 May 1793 to 25 July 1801; Humayun Shah ruled as a rival at Kandahar from May 1793 to December 1795.

rulers.name: Ayub Shah
rulers.note: December 1818 to 1823; deposed in the Kabul fighting after the Battle of Nowshera. Shuja Shah's second reign (1839-42) belongs to the durrani-dynasty dossier.

ledger.note: 1747: Ahmad Shah Durrani is crowned at Kandahar. Reign 'from 23 July 1747'; he 'encamped in Naderabad and prepared to be crowned king' near Kandahar and took Ghazni 'with little opposition'. The Durrani page says 'Empire established by Ahmad Shah Durrani: July 1747' after a loya jirga in June 1747. The page names the cities, not a boundary.

October 1747: Kabul is handed over. 'When Ahmad Shah arrived at Kabul in October 1747, the Qizilbash garrison handed over the Bala Hissar fortress.' The Durrani page: 'wrest Kabul and Peshawar from Mughal-appointed governor Nasir Khan'.
1748: Peshawar falls. 'The Afghan armies approached Peshawar' and Nasir Khan fled; the page gives 1747-48 without a month.
January 1748: the first Afghan campaign into the Punjab. 'Afghans won the battle of Lahore on 11 January 1748'; the Mughals held the Punjab until the treaty of 1752.

region.text: Sindh under the Kalhora dynasty, paying tribute

ledger.note: 1749: Sindh enters Afghan suzerainty. 'The Mughal Emperor Ahmad Shah Bahadur was induced to cede Sindh, the Punjab region' (1749); the Ahmad Shah page dates Sindh's entry into 'Afghan suzerainty' to 1747 and the Punjab annexation to the treaty of 3 April 1752. Drawn as a vassal, not as direct land.

Late 1750: Herat falls after a long siege. 'Herat finally fell in late 1750.' The page does not name the defender; the Shahrokh Shah page has the Afghans take Herat 'after a siege lasting several months' in the Afsharid restoration.
November 1750: the first siege of Mashhad. The siege 'was lifted in November 1750'; the page also has a failed assault on Nishapur in 1750-51, and no ground was held until 1754-55.

region.text: Srinagar and the province of Kashmir

ledger.note: 1752: Kashmir. 'Shah Pasand Khan's force quickly occupied Srinagar and established complete control in the province', the campaign following the Punjab conquest; the page gives the year by sequence.

region.text: the Maimana Khanate (Faryab), an ally under Ahmad Shah's protection

ledger.note: Summer 1752: the northern Uzbek khanate. 'by the summer of 1752, the forces of the alliance were victorious' and 'Balkh was restored to the rule of the Maimana Khanate'; Hajji Bi had sought Ahmad Shah's aid in 1751. Afghan authority north of the Hindu Kush rests on this alliance. Faryab is the khanate's own land and is drawn as vassal land (out of the keyframes); Balkh is entered as Durrani land in the next event. [Repaired after review ia-03-e: the region text said Balkh stayed under Maimana until 1768, and the quote was not verbatim.]

region.text: Balkh, restored with Hajji Bi of Maimana as Ahmad Shah's governor

ledger.note: By summer 1752: Balkh passes from the Qataghanids to Hajji Bi under Ahmad Shah. 'Coming into conflict against Hazara Bi, the ruler of Qataghan, Hajji Bi lost control over Balkh to the Qataghanids.'; 'In 1751, Hajji Bi travelled to Herat with a delegation of amirs, seeking Ahmad Shah's aid to reclaim Balkh.'; 'by the summer of 1752, the forces of the alliance were victorious'; 'Balkh was restored to the rule of the Maimana Khanate'. 'Hajji Bi was also bestowed by Ahmad Shah with the titles of governor of Balkh and tax collector.' In 1755-1756 'Ahmad Shah also declared a new governor of Balkh, Nawab Khan Alakozai.' Entered as Durrani land from 1752 because the governor holds it under Ahmad Shah's titles; the page does not call it an annexation and gives no month, hence confidence 2. [Repaired after review ia-03-e: replaces the 1768 'gain' from khanate-of-bukhara, which had the wrong year and the wrong counterpart; 1768 is the contest below.]

3 April 1752: the Punjab passes to the Afghans. A treaty signed by Bahadur Shah 'officiated the annexation of Punjab, including Multan, Lahore, and areas up to Sirhind, ending Mughal rule there'; Moin-ul-Mulk was defeated on 6 March 1752.

region.text: Multan, Lahore and the areas up to Sirhind

ledger.note: 3 April 1752: the Punjab, Multan and Lahore to Sirhind. The Afghans seized Lahore again 'with little resistance' on 20 December 1756.
1753: Badakhshan is subjugated. 'After the Qataghan revolt was put down, Badakhshan was subjugated as well.'
1 December 1754: Mashhad surrenders. 'The Afsharids submitted on 1 December 1754.'

region.text: Mashhad and Khorasan under Shahrokh Shah, a Durrani protectorate

ledger.note: 9 May 1755: Shahrokh Shah is restored at Mashhad 'as a Durrani protectorate'. Drawn as a vassal; the Cliopatria shape includes Mashhad from 1752.

region.text: Nishapur under Abbas Quli of the Qara Bayat Amirdom, allowed to return 'as governor of the city'

ledger.note: 17 June 1755: Nishapur submits. 'Nonetheless, after the siege of Mashhad, Ahmad Shah advanced to Nishapur, which was ruled by the Qara Bayat Amirdom.'; 'On 17 June 1755, the Afghan armies arrived at Nishapur, resulting in Abbas Quli's immediate submission.' The gates were then closed, 'the Afghans laid siege for one week', 'The city was then plundered', and 'Abbas Quli was allowed to return to Nishapur as governor of the city.' So the city stays under its own ruler as a Durrani vassal, not a conquest from the Afsharids; it is not drawn as direct land. Nishapur also lies inside the Razavi Khorasan region of /ledger/13 (Shahrokh Shah's Mashhad) and is entered again here because its own ruler, not Shahrokh Shah, submitted. [Repaired after review ia-03-e: was a 'gain' from afsharid-iran whose quote 'took the city' is not on the page.]

region.text: the Khanate of Kalat under Mir Nasir Khan

ledger.note: 1758: Kalat. After besieging Kalat for forty days Ahmad Shah 'reaffirmed Nasir Khan in his position' under a treaty requiring recognition of his suzerainty. The Kalat page says accounts conflict: 'Since 1748, Kalat was a vassal state of Durrani Empire', 'Kalat did not pay any tribute to Durrani Empire thereafter', and 'some sources state that the Khanate of Kalat became a sovereign state'.

region.text: the Punjab from Lahore to Delhi

ledger.note: 1759: the Afghans reach Lahore to meet the Marathas. 'By 1759 Ahmad Shah and his army had reached Lahore and were poised to confront the Marathas', who had brought 'Lahore, Multan, Kashmir and other subahs on the Indian side of Attock under Maratha rule'.

region.text: the Punjab and the road to Delhi

ledger.note: 14 January 1761: Panipat. 'The Third Battle of Panipat: the Durranis decisively defeated the Marathas.' The Bukharans withdrew across the Amu Darya the same year after their defeat at Aqcha (Ahmad Shah page).

region.text: the Punjab around Lahore and Amritsar

ledger.note: 1762: the Sikh war. Ahmad's sixth crossing into India 'to subdue the Sikhs'; 'Durrani's forces instigated the Vaddha Ghallughara when they killed thousands of Sikhs in the Punjab in 1762' and sacked Amritsar.

region.text: the regions between Tashkent and Kokand

ledger.note: 1763: Ahmad Shah 'occupied the regions between Tashkent and Kokand, withdrawing by 1764'. Cliopatria does not show it; Tashkent was independent and the Kokand Khanate is the counterpart named here as the nearest state.

region.text: the regions between Tashkent and Kokand

ledger.note: 1764: the Afghans withdraw from the Tashkent-Kokand lands ('withdrawing by 1764').

1767: the last of Ahmad Shah's Indian invasions. The Ahmad Shah page's infobox lists the seventh (1764-65) and eighth (1766-67) invasions after the sixth of 1762; the Punjab then lies in Sikh hands (next event).

region.text: Balkh and the northern frontier on the Amu Darya

ledger.note: 1768: Shah Murad Manghit of Bukhara invades. 'In 1768, a rebellion in Qataghan and Badakhshan prompted an invasion from Shah Murad Manghit, the next Bukharan ruler.' Ahmad Shah advanced 'affirming his authority in Maimana, Andkhoy, Sheberghan, and Balkh'. Moves no land: Balkh was already Durrani from 1752. [Repaired after review ia-03-e: replaces a 1768 'gain' of Balkh from khanate-of-bukhara at confidence 3 that had the wrong year and the wrong counterpart; khanate-of-bukhara needs no 1768 loss, only the matching contest events.]

region.text: Balkh and the Amu Darya frontier

ledger.note: 1768: Shah Murad negotiates and 'recognized Afghan control over Balkh' (Ahmad Shah page; the paragraph is dated 1768, the exact month is not given). The Durrani Empire page adds that Ahmad Shah and the Uzbek Emir 'agreed that the Amu Darya would mark the division of their lands' (no year on that page). No land changes hands.

1769 or 1770: Badakhshan is occupied. 'Within the year, Ahmad Shah occupied Badakhshan and Sultan Shah was executed' (Durrani page; the sentence follows Sultan Shah's letter of December 1769, so the page does not fix the year; the invasion began under Shah Wali Khan in May 1768 and took Fayzabad); the vassal becomes direct land. [Reviewer ia-03-e: confidence lowered from 3 and quote corrected, the page does not say 'Within 1769'.]

1769 or 1770: Badakhshan is annexed after Sultan Shah's execution ('Within the year', after his December 1769 letter, Durrani page); Sultan Shah had sought Qing help after the 1759 pressure. [Reviewer ia-03-e: confidence lowered from 3, year not stated on the page.]

region.text: the Indian Punjab and Sirhind lands in Cliopatria's 1771 shape and not in 1772

ledger.note: 1772: the eastern Punjab goes to the Sikhs. 'He had lost parts of Punjab to the Sikhs' at Ahmad Shah's death (16/17 October 1772); the Timur Shah page adds 'the Sikhs conquered Multan in 1772' and that the Sikhs were 'in possession of the provinces of Lahore and Multan' when Timur Shah acceded. Cliopatria's 1772 shape drops 1,308 India cells, the region given here.
1776: the capital moves from Kandahar to Kabul, with Peshawar as winter capital (infobox 'Kandahar (1747-1776); Kabul (1776-1823); Peshawar as winter capital (1776-1823)').
1783: the Kalhora dynasty falls. 'The Talpur dynasty was established in 1783 by Mir Fateh Ali Khan' after the Battle of Halani; the Talpurs then 'paid tribute' to the Durrani.

1783: the Talpurs rule Sindh as tributaries. 'For most of their rule, they were subordinate or subject to the Durrani Empire and paid tribute to them'; 'nominally under the Afghan kings, until the British conquest'. The Zaman Shah page says Sindh 'had severed itself' in the 1790s and was spared 'on condition they would tribute to the Durrani Empire once again'.

region.text: Kashmir under the rebel governor Azad Khan

ledger.note: After 1783: Azad Khan, governor of Kashmir, 'rebelled after 1783 and stopped sending revenue to Kabul'.
11 December 1786: the Kashmir rebellion ends and 'Kashmir was reabsorbed under firm imperial control'.
May 1793: Humayun Mirza rebels at Kandahar against Zaman Shah ('Humayun Shah (rival, Kandahar): May 1793 - Dec 1795'); the civil war began on 20 May 1793.
December 1795: Humayun is defeated at Qalati Ghilji and flees; Zaman Shah later had him executed (Zaman Shah page).

1796: Mashhad falls to the Qajar. Agha Mohammad Shah 'reached Mashhad as part of his conquest of Khorasan'; Shahrokh Shah 'died at Damghan' in 1796 of his tortures. The page gives no year for the entry into Mashhad; Cliopatria drops Mashhad and Nishapur from the Durrani shape in 1797.

1796: Nishapur goes with Mashhad in the Qajar conquest of Khorasan. The pages never mention Nishapur after 1755; the end follows Cliopatria's 1797 shape (Mashhad and Nishapur leave in 1797) and Shahrokh Shah's death in 1796. The Agha Mohammad Khan page (opened for the repair) does not mention Nishapur: it has only 'A year after Agha Mohammad Khan re-subjugated the Caucasus, he also captured Khorasan' and that he 'entered Mashhad on 14 May' (no year given). [Repaired after review ia-03-e: was a 'loss' to qajar-dynasty, replaced by the end of the Nishapur vassalage.]

1818: Herat becomes the seat of Mahmud Shah and Kamran Shah. 'In 1818, Mahmud and later Kamran Shah took over' at Herat, which the Herat page treats as a separate principality 'from 1793 to 1863'; the Durrani page's infobox keeps 'Herat (1793-1863)' as a capital, so the page set conflicts.
1818: Multan. 'Multan was conquered in 1818, which ended Afghan influence in Punjab.'

1818: Kalat's tribute passes from the Durrani throne to the new Principality of Kandahar. The Kandahar page says Sindh and Balochistan 'paid tribute and were dependent on the principality', and that they 'were able to break away in August 1826 following the death of Sher Dil Khan'; the principality was founded in August 1818. The page does not date the transfer; the year is the founding year. The Kalat page's 'any trace of Afghan influence over Kalat ended after the death of Sher Dil Khan' (1826) agrees. [Repaired after review ia-03-e: was dated 1823 at confidence 1.]

1818: Sindh's tribute passes from the Durrani throne to the new Principality of Kandahar (same page quotes as the Kalat event; Sindh broke away in August 1826). The Talpur page has Sindh nominally Afghan until 1843, which this dossier does not follow beyond 1823 because Kabul no longer held the suzerainty. [Repaired after review ia-03-e: was dated 1823 at confidence 1.]
August 1818: Kandahar breaks away. The Principality of Kandahar was 'founded by Sher Dil Khan in August 1818 as a breakaway from the Durrani Empire'.
3 July 1819: Shopian. 'After the battle of Shopian, Ranjit Singh successfully defeated the Afghans and annexed the Kashmir Valley.'
1823: the Maimana Khanate passes to the Barakzai orbit; the Emirate page lists the Maimana Khanate among the Emirate's predecessors.

14 March 1823: Nowshera. The Sikhs under Ranjit Singh beat Mohammad Azim Khan and Peshawar stayed 'under a tributary arrangement', with a Sikh garrison in the citadel; the Sikh Empire page says Peshawar 'became tributary in 1823' and was 'formally annexed in 1834'.

March 1823: the Durrani Empire ends at Kabul. 'Fall of Kabul in March 1823' (Durrani infobox); 'Ayub Shah was deposed and presumably killed. Kabul fell in March 1823, and the Barakzai dynasty superseded the Durrani'; the Emirate page's infobox has 'Established: 1823'. Herat stays with the Sadozai (Mahmud and Kamran) until 1863.

correction.text: Kandahar (crowned near it 23 July 1747), Ghazni ('conquering it with little opposition') and Kabul (October 1747)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Durrani shape starts in 1748, but the empire was founded in July 1747. Kandahar and Ghazni came first; Kabul was handed over in October 1747 ('when Ahmad Shah arrived at Kabul in October 1747, the Qizilbash garrison handed over the Bala Hissar'). The shape is the year-end state of 1747.

correction.text: Kandahar, Ghazni, Kabul and the Peshawar valley, the lands taken 1747-48

keyframe_review.note: 54,363 km2 (2.5% of the later peak), the Kabul province alone (192 cells, Kabul 100%). The page puts Kandahar, Ghazni and Kabul in 1747 and Peshawar in 1747-48 ('Nasir Khan fled as the Afghan armies approached Peshawar'); Herat only fell in late 1750 (see the next keyframe). Holds for 1748-1749 as corrected.

correction.text: the 1748 core plus Herat, which 'finally fell in late 1750'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Herat 'finally fell in late 1750' after a long siege, so the shape for 1750-1751 adds Herat to the four cities of 1748. The two sieges of Mashhad (November 1750, lifted) took no ground. Cliopatria's 1748 shape ends in 1751 and its 1752 shape already contains Herat and Mashhad.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape without the Murghab oasis around Merv, Razavi Khorasan (Mashhad, Nishapur: a protectorate from 1755), Sindh, Baluchistan and the Maimana lands in Faryab (vassals), with the whole Punjab (to Sirhind), Kashmir and Balkh added

keyframe_review.note: 0.97 M km2 for 1752-1756. The shape has Herat, Kandahar, Kabul, Peshawar and Mashhad but only 11% of Pakistani Punjab and no Multan or Kashmir; the page has the Punjab 'including Multan, Lahore, and areas up to Sirhind' by the treaty of 3 April 1752 and Kashmir occupied 'just after'. Mashhad only surrendered on 1 December 1754 and became a protectorate on 9 May 1755, so the Cliopatria shape is early there; Merv was under Qajar governors until 1785 (Merv page: 'In 1608, Mihrab Khan Qajar became governor, beginning two centuries of Qajar governorship over Merv'), so the Murghab oasis in the shape is not Durrani. Sindh and Baluchistan inside this shape are vassal land (ledger: Kalhora then Talpur Sindh, Kalat), not direct territory. Faryab, the Maimana Khanate's land (ledger: vassal from 1752), is taken out for the same reason. Balkh is added whole: it passed to Ahmad Shah's governor by summer 1752 (ledger), and Cliopatria's 1752 shape has only 11 of its 54 cells.

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape without the Murghab oasis around Merv, Razavi Khorasan (Mashhad, Nishapur: a protectorate from 1755), Sindh, Baluchistan, the Maimana lands in Faryab and Badakhshan (vassals; Badakhshan until 1769), with the whole Punjab (to Sirhind) and Kashmir added

keyframe_review.note: 1.41 M km2 for 1757-1761: adds Kunduz, Badakhshan, Balkh and a third of Indian Punjab to the 1752 shape. Same corrections as 1752: the Punjab and Kashmir were taken in 1752 and the shape lacks Kashmir until 1762; Merv is not Durrani. Delhi was sacked in January 1757 but Alamgir II 'was kept as a vassal' and no land was annexed. Sindh and Baluchistan inside this shape are vassal land (ledger: Kalhora then Talpur Sindh, Kalat), not direct territory. Faryab, the Maimana Khanate's land (ledger: vassal from 1752), is taken out for the same reason. Badakhshan, a vassal from 1753 until its annexation in 1769 or 1770 (ledger), is taken out until then. Of the three Cliopatria additions, Balkh is Durrani from 1752 (ledger) and Badakhshan is a vassal until 1769 (taken out). Kunduz (with Takhar and Baghlan, the Qataghan lands) stays in as direct land, unverified: the Ahmad Shah page has only the revolt of Mizrab Bi, son of Hazara Bi, put down in 1753 with Afghan help, and the Durrani Empire page has 'the Afghans established Sarimsaq, a child of the Afaqi's who escaped to Badakhshan, in Kunduz' (no year); neither gives the status or a date.

union.text: Rajasthan: Bikaner, Marwar, Jaisalmer and the other Rajput states

correction.text: Cliopatria's shape without the Murghab oasis around Merv, Razavi Khorasan (Mashhad, Nishapur: a protectorate from 1755), Sindh, Baluchistan, the Maimana lands in Faryab and Badakhshan (vassals; Badakhshan until 1769); fx-12: without Rajasthan

keyframe_review.note: 2.13 M km2: the largest extent begins, with Kashmir, the Punjab and Multan whole. The infobox gives 'about 2,000,000 km2' (no year), so the raw shape is 1.07 times the infobox; after removing the vassals, Merv and Mashhad the corrected shape is about 1.5 M km2 (ratio 0.74). The Sirhind lands in the east are in the shape but the pages never say the Afghans held them beyond the 1752 treaty line. Sindh and Baluchistan inside this shape are vassal land (ledger: Kalhora then Talpur Sindh, Kalat), not direct territory. Faryab, the Maimana Khanate's land (ledger: vassal from 1752), is taken out for the same reason. Badakhshan, a vassal from 1753 until its annexation in 1769 or 1770 (ledger), is taken out until then. Kunduz, Takhar and Baghlan stay in as direct land, unverified (see the 1757 keyframe). fx-12 (2026-11-01), hierarchy fixes F210 F218 F228: Rajasthan is taken out of this outline. The Durrani page never names Rajasthan, Bikaner, Jodhpur, Marwar or Jaisalmer, and bounds Ahmad Shah's 1757 settlement at Afghan 'suzerainty over the regions south of the Indus River, up to the Sutlej River' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durrani_Empire); the Bikaner State page (Gaj Singh 1746-1787, Surat Singh 1787-1828) and the Kingdom of Marwar page (Bijay Singh 1752-1793, 'overrun by the Maratha hordes') name no Durrani tie (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bikaner_State, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Marwar), and the Jaisalmer State page has 'Mughals controlled the fort until 1762' and the Bhati rulers after it, no Durrani (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaisalmer_State). Cliopatria's outline reaches into the Thar only in 1762-1771 (about 900 Rajasthan cells) and 1772-1819 (about 50, the Jaisalmer border).

wars.name: Durrani invasions of the Punjab (Mughal campaigns)
wars.outcome: Durrani victory: the treaty of 3 April 1752 annexed the Punjab with Multan and Lahore to Sirhind and Kashmir followed.
wars.note: The Durrani Empire page dates the cession of Sindh and the Punjab to 1749.

wars.name: Durrani campaigns in Khorasan
wars.outcome: Herat fell in late 1750; Mashhad surrendered on 1 December 1754 and Shahrokh Shah was restored on 9 May 1755 as a Durrani protectorate; Nishapur submitted on 17 June 1755 and its ruler Abbas Quli stayed on as governor (a vassal, not a conquest).

wars.name: Durrani conquest of Afghan Turkestan
wars.outcome: Balkh taken back from the Qataghanids under Hajji Bi as Ahmad Shah's governor (summer 1752), Badakhshan subjugated (1753), Bukharans pushed back across the Amu Darya (1761), Balkh recognised as Afghan by Shah Murad (1768), Badakhshan occupied (1769).
wars.note: The Durrani page gives the Badakhshan invasion as May 1768 (Shah Wali Khan, Fayzabad) and the occupation 'Within the year' after Sultan Shah's letter of December 1769 (1769 or 1770); the 1768 meeting with Shah Murad moved no land.

wars.name: Siege of Kalat (1758)
wars.outcome: Ahmad Shah besieged Kalat for over forty days, failed to storm it, and 'reaffirmed Nasir Khan in his position' under a treaty of suzerainty; the Kalat page says Kalat paid no tribute afterwards.
wars.note: The Kalat page says Nasir Khan 'revolted against Ahmad Shah' in 1758.

wars.name: Third Battle of Panipat
wars.outcome: Durrani victory on 14 January 1761; the Punjab and Kashmir stayed Afghan.

wars.name: Durrani-Sikh wars (1762-1767)
wars.outcome: The Vadda Ghallughara (1762) and the invasions of 1764-65 and 1766-67 did not hold the Punjab; by 1772 'he had lost parts of Punjab to the Sikhs'.

wars.name: Azad Khan's revolt in Kashmir
wars.outcome: The governor Azad Khan stopped sending revenue after 1783; the revolt ended on 11 December 1786 and Kashmir was reabsorbed.

wars.name: Durrani civil war (Zaman Shah to Ayub Shah)
wars.outcome: Humayun's revolt at Kandahar (May 1793 to December 1795), Zaman Shah's overthrow by Mahmud Shah (25 July 1801), and the reigns of Shuja, Mahmud, Ali and Ayub ended with the breakup of 1818.
wars.note: The page notes that 25 July 1801 'was not the end of civil strife' and that by 1818 the Sadozai held little beyond Kabul.

wars.name: Qajar conquest of Khorasan (1796)
wars.outcome: Agha Mohammad Shah took Mashhad and Shahrokh Shah died in 1796; the Durrani protectorate over Khorasan ended.
wars.note: The page gives no year for the entry into Mashhad.

wars.name: Afghan-Sikh wars (1818-1823)
wars.outcome: Sikh victories: Multan (1818), Kashmir at Shopian (3 July 1819), Nowshera (14 March 1823) leaving Peshawar tributary.
wars.note: The Sikh Empire page: Peshawar 'became tributary in 1823' and was 'formally annexed in 1834'.

certainty.note: Frontiers are approximate throughout. The Amu Darya line with Bukhara, agreed between Ahmad Shah and the Emir (the Durrani Empire page gives no year; the Ahmad Shah page has Shah Murad recognise Afghan control over Balkh in 1768), is a river line; the Punjab line to Sirhind follows the 1752 treaty but the pages give no survey.

notes: Cliopatria's Durrani Empire runs 1748..1827; the Wikipedia article ends the empire with the fall of Kabul in March 1823 and starts the Emirate of Afghanistan in 1823, so this dossier ends in 1823 and Cliopatria's 1825 shape (1825-1827) is marked wrong. Pages disagree: the Durrani Empire page dates the cession of Sindh and the Punjab to 1749, Ahmad Shah's own page dates the Punjab to the treaty of 3 April 1752; the Kalat page says both that Kalat was a vassal from 1748 and that it became sovereign in 1758; the Talpur page has the Talpurs nominally subject to the Afghans to 1843 while the Principality of Kandahar page has Sindh and Baluchistan breaking away in August 1826 (after this dossier's end); the Herat page treats Herat as a separate principality since 1793 while the Durrani infobox lists Herat as a capital 1793-1863. Cliopatria problems: the 1748-1751 shape is the Kabul province alone; the 1752-1790 shapes include the Merv oasis (Mary, Lebap, Ahal in Turkmenistan), which the Merv page shows under Qajar governors until Shah Murad in 1785; Sindh and Baluchistan are drawn as direct territory (they are vassals in the ledger); the 1820-1827 shapes keep Kandahar, Herat, Peshawar and Gilgit long after the pages show them gone, and the 1822/1825 outline is identical to the Emirate's 1828 shape. Unverified within the page budget: the exact date Mashhad and Nishapur were lost (1796 is Shahrokh's death); Sirhind and the eastern Punjab, which Cliopatria holds to 1771 and the pages never describe; Multan between 1772 and 1818; the Hindu Kush frontier of Kunduz and Badakhshan. Counterparts that need dossiers: kalhora-dynasty (Sindh to 1783), khanate-of-kalat, maimana-khanate, mirdom-of-badakhshan, principality-of-kandahar, principality-of-herat (all Cliopatria-less), plus Azad Khan's Kashmir rebellion and Humayun Mirza's rival rule as rebels of two to three years that need no dossier. Page budget: 9 pages were opened for this state (Durrani Empire, Ahmad Shah, Timur Shah, Sikh Empire, Talpur, Kalat, Shahrokh Shah, Nowshera, Zaman Shah); the Kandahar, Herat, Merv and Emirate pages were opened for the neighbouring dossiers of this batch and are reused here at no extra cost. Gazetteer: 'Kashmir Valley', 'Punjab', 'Sind', 'Baluchistan', 'Mary', 'Razavi Khorasan', 'Hirat' and the places Kabul, Peshawar, Multan, Nishapur (as Neyshabur) and Khujand were used as found. Repaired after review ia-03-e (2026-10-19): Balkh is a gain of summer 1752 from the Qataghanids (the 1768 'gain' from Bukhara became a contest pair that moves no land); Nishapur is a vassal under its own Qara Bayat ruler 1755-1796; Faryab (Maimana) is taken out of the 1752-1811 keyframes as vassal land and Badakhshan out of 1757-1763 until its annexation; Kunduz stays in as unverified; the Kalat and Sindh vassal ends move to 1818 (the Principality of Kandahar page); the Lahore and Multan holdings 1772-1818 and the north before 1818 remain unverified (the Timur Shah and Mahmud Shah pages are silent on who held them). fx-12 (2026-11-01): Rajasthan was taken out of the 1762-1811 outlines (Bikaner, Marwar, Jaisalmer: no page gives the Durrani any Rajasthani land) and the Bahawalpur country out of the outlines from 1802 (new one-year keyframe durrani-empire_1802; the 1800 keyframe now ends in 1801). The 1752 and 1757 outlines hold only Punjab (Pakistan) cells of the Bikaner and Jaisalmer circles, Bahawalpur land, and were left.
